problem_text:
A logistics center must devise a procurement and storage schedule for a critical component over a 10-day operational window.  
The initial stock available at the start of the planning interval is 15 units.  
For each day t = 1, ..., 10, the vendor permits the center to submit a procurement request, the size of which must fall between 12 and 42 units.  
Nevertheless, every request issued will experience a 3-day transit delay before it becomes available to meet requirements or augment the stock level.  
The required usage of the component each day is as follows:  
* Day 1: requirement 59 units  
* Day 2: requirement 44 units  
* Day 3: requirement 46 units  
* Day 4: requirement 45 units  
* Day 5: requirement 26 units  
* Day 6: requirement 53 units  
* Day 7: requirement 12 units  
* Day 8: requirement 39 units  
* Day 9: requirement 35 units  
* Day 10: requirement 56 units  

Stockouts are tolerated, though any unsatisfied requirement is considered lost and will not be fulfilled later.  
Throughout the 10-day horizon, component quantities may be treated as continuous values, and the total physical stock on the premises at any moment must not surpass the storage limit of 57 units.  

On the first day, the maximum allowable procurement quantity is restricted to 20 units.  
By the conclusion of day 10, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 44 units.  

The aggregate expenditure across the planning span comprises three elements: the procurement expense, charged at 1 per unit requested; the storage expense, charged at 1 per unit held over from one day to the next; and the shortage penalty, levied at 10 per unit of unfulfilled requirement.  
The objective is to identify the optimal procurement quantity each day and to monitor the ensuing stock and shortage levels so as to minimize the total expenditure.
